_about: Carbon facts for the CBAM comparison and the carbon passports. Researched 23 Nov 2026 from the sources given; figures marked 'second-hand' were read from secondary copies of the regulation and must be checked against the Official Journal before any real use.

cbam.covers_source: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 Annex I lists heading 7318 (screws, bolts, nuts, rivets, washers of iron or steel); wording read from Council doc ST-16973-2025-ADD-1 (Dec 2025), second-hand
cbam.de_minimis_source: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 (20 Oct 2025): importers under 50 t a year of CBAM goods are exempt
cbam.certificate_source: European Commission, CBAM certificate price Q3 2026 (EUR 82.32/tCO2e, published 5 Oct 2026); Q1 75.36, Q2 75.28
cbam.charged_share_source: Free allocation phase-out mirrored by CBAM: 2.5% charged in 2026 rising to 100% in 2034 (Regulation (EU) 2023/956 with the ETS reform); a 2026 Commission proposal, not adopted, would stretch it to 2038
cbam.china_default_source: Default value for CN 7318 15 (threaded screws and bolts) from China: 6.375 tCO2e/t before mark-up; 7.01 (2026), 7.65 (2027), 8.29 (2028) with mark-up. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 as corrected by 2026/1740; second-hand via cbamdefaults.com

steel_routes.source: worldsteel Sustainability Indicators 2025 (2024 data, CO2 only); Italy made 89.3% of its steel in electric-arc furnaces in 2024 (EU 44.4%); China under 10% EAF (CREA 2026)

electricity_source: Italian grid average, about 0.25 kgCO2/kWh (ISPRA, estimate)
pcf_standard: Catena-X Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) rulebook: the fields below follow its main ones; Tier-1s such as BMW use it with suppliers
